name: mcp__lens_studio__RecompileTypeScriptTool
description: Triggers a forced TypeScript recompilation. Returns { status: 'succeeded' | 'failed', errors?: string[], logFile?: string }. On failure, the inline `errors` array contains compiler error messages — read those directly. IMPORTANT: `status: 'succeeded'` means the TypeScript compiler passed — it does NOT mean the Lens runs. A scene that compiles cleanly can still crash at runtime (`Cannot find asset:`, `Input X was not provided`, missing built-in references, reset loops). After a `succeeded` recompile, ALWAYS follow with `RunAndCollectLogsTool` to verify runtime. Skipping this step is the most common cause of agents reporting success on broken scenes.
inputSchema:
exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__lens_studio__RecompileTypeScriptTool(args: { [key: string]: unknown; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

name: mcp__lens_studio__list_leaf_scenarios
description: List all LEAF scenarios registered by the lens on the current execution target, with their default configuration parameters. Use before run_leaf_scenario to discover valid scenarioId values.

name: mcp__lens_studio__push_leaf_lens
description: Push the current project's lens to the paired Spectacles device and, when 'Execute on device' is enabled, wait for it to become ready and reload the scenario list from it. Use to (re)deploy the lens after code changes; run_leaf_scenario only auto-pushes when no lens is running on the device.
inputSchema:
exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__lens_studio__push_leaf_lens(args: { [key: string]: unknown; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

name: mcp__lens_studio__run_leaf_scenario
description: Run a LEAF integration-test scenario in the currently-open Lens Studio project. The LEAF panel must be open before calling this tool (it owns the lens bridge). Returns the final status reported by the lens once the scenario completes.
